FINDING_ID: IM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76
DESCRIPTION: `apply_diagnosis()` runs the damping check before it knows which remediation chain/parameter a diagnosis maps to, and keys damping on `diagnosis.detector`. This is already known in the general sense, but a missed consequence remains: outcome diagnoses from `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` do not count as adjustments, so a failed step can escalate the chain and then the very next fresh diagnosis from a *different detector string* that maps into the same chain can immediately re-enter `apply_diagnosis()` and apply the escalated step without any parameter-level cooldown. The damping mechanism is therefore bypassable by alternate detector labels or chain mappings, not just semantically mis-scoped. This matters because `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS` is parameter-oriented (`tau_sim`, `tau_vocab_growth`, directives), while damping is detector-oriented and checked before mapping.
PROPOSED_FIX: Resolve diagnosis to `chain_key` and target parameter first, then enforce damping on a canonical remediation identity such as `(parameter)` or `(chain_key, parameter)`. Record deferred/escalated/remediation-state transitions against that same identity so all paths share one cooldown.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: `apply_diagnosis()` can silently discard a pathology forever when `recommended_chain_start()` returns an index beyond the available chain length. The method rewrites `chain_idx = recommended_start`, then immediately checks `if chain_idx >= len(chain):` and records chain exhaustion. Because `recommended_chain_start()` derives from historical step effectiveness and can return `last_skipped + 1`, duplicate/aliased transforms or bad step statistics can push the suggested start past the chain end even when some steps were never actually tried for the current episode. That converts heuristic learning into hard exhaustion.
PROPOSED_FIX: Clamp `recommended_start` to the highest valid untried step for the current chain, or only skip within `[0, len(chain)-1]`. Distinguish “historically skip this step” from “chain exhausted for this incident.”
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67
DESCRIPTION: `false_positive_rate` treats every non-`remediation_outcome` diagnosis in `self._diagnoses` as a “detection,” including derived informational/self-generated diagnoses like `self_diagnosis`, repeated dispatch diagnoses, and per-model anomalies. But `record_natural_resolution()` is only called for a narrow subset of pathologies whose counters are explicitly reset in `record_round()` / `record_model_round()`. Many detectors contribute to the denominator but can never contribute to the numerator because they have no natural-resolution recording path. The rate is therefore structurally biased downward even aside from the known window mismatch.
PROPOSED_FIX: Restrict the denominator to diagnosis families that participate in natural-resolution accounting, or add symmetric resolution tracking for every detector class included in the metric.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: `record_model_round()` never resolves or decays `model_failure_*` pathology state when a model recovers. It resets `_model_failure_counts[model_id] = 0` on success, but leaves `_pathology_counts[f"model_failure_{model_id}"]` untouched. As a result, persistence/occurrence for model-failure diagnoses is monotone across the whole run, so later isolated failure streaks inherit stale severity escalation from old incidents instead of being treated as new episodes.
PROPOSED_FIX: On a non-failed round, if `model_failure_{model_id}` was active, increment `_resolved_counts`, optionally record natural resolution when no remediation is active, and reset `_pathology_counts[key] = 0`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60
DESCRIPTION: `record_model_round()` has the same missing-resolution problem for `parser_yield_{model_id}` and `cpf_spike_{model_id}`. Both counters are incremented when diagnosed, but unlike `monotonic_decline_{model_id}`, neither has an `else` branch to mark recovery and clear the pathology count once the signal disappears. This makes persistence counts sticky and prevents false-positive/natural-resolution accounting for these pathologies.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add explicit recovery branches for `parser_yield` and `cpf_spike` analogous to `monotonic_decline`, including `_resolved_counts`, optional `record_natural_resolution`, and `_pathology_counts[key] = 0`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.81
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73
DESCRIPTION: `approve_deferred_remediation()` applies a deferred fix using the original diagnosis round for both `_record_adjustment(..., round_idx)` and `set_remediation_state(applied_round=round_idx)`. This is known at a high level as backdating, but the missed immune-specific consequence is that approval late in the run can cause `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` to verify the newly approved fix immediately or on the next round using a verification window that has already “elapsed” on paper before the fix ever took effect. That corrupts remediation outcome attribution and can spur immediate false escalation.
PROPOSED_FIX: Use the approval-time round, not the original diagnosis round, for both adjustment logging and remediation-state `applied_round`. Preserve original diagnosis round in separate metadata only.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.69
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: `apply_diagnosis()` handles `mu+novelty` disagreement by emitting an “adjustment” to pseudo-parameter `stop_signal_priority`, but no actual configuration or behavior changes anywhere. A related finding exists, but the missed part is that this inert pseudo-adjustment is still recorded in `_immune_adjustments`, so it participates in damping. That means a no-op advisory can suppress future real diagnoses from the same detector within `immune_damping_rounds`, wasting the immune feedback channel.
PROPOSED_FIX: Do not record advisory/no-op responses as immune adjustments. Either implement a real configurable stop-signal policy or emit a non-adjustment event that does not enter damping state.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F008
SEVERITY: 0.66
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: `check_dispatch_health()` can emit repeated verification-miscalibration diagnoses every round for the same model because `_pathology_counts[key]` is only used to increase severity, not to gate duplicate emission. Since `apply_diagnosis()` for verification writes a directive only if none exists, once the first directive is present later diagnoses become operationally inert but continue to accumulate in `_diagnoses`, skewing self-metrics and event volume.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add episode gating: only emit a fresh verification miscalibration diagnosis on threshold crossing or after prior resolution. Alternatively track active pathology state per model and suppress duplicates until recovery.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F009
SEVERITY: 0.77
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: `self_diagnose()` adjusts `_sensitivity_decay` in response to high false-positive rate, but `effective_window()` does not use `_sensitivity_decay` at all. Existing findings note this broadly, but the missed stronger point is that this makes Self-check 2's “adjustment” a full internal no-op while still being logged as successful self-adaptation and influencing future `fp_improving` logic through `_self_diagnosis_history`. The subsystem can therefore self-corroborate phantom adaptation.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either incorporate `_sensitivity_decay` into `effective_window()`/pathology sensitivity calculations, or remove Self-check 2 auto-adjustment and treat it as a human-review diagnostic until the parameter has an actual effect path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F010
SEVERITY: 0.64
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: `record_round()` appends verification outcome diagnoses from `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` to the returned `new_diagnoses`, but does not add them to `self._diagnoses`. Meanwhile other diagnoses are appended to `self._diagnoses` before return. This creates an inconsistent diagnosis ledger: event consumers see remediation outcomes, but internal analytics using `self._diagnoses` do not. That asymmetry undermines any metric or audit that expects `all_diagnoses` to be complete.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either append verification outcome diagnoses to `self._diagnoses` as well, or explicitly define them as external-only events and exclude them consistently from all internal accounting.
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: these are additional missed immune-layer findings beyond the supplied prior set, with the strongest new issues being canonical-identity damping bypass, learned-start false exhaustion, unresolved per-model pathology state, and approval-time backdating corrupting remediation verification.
